- Datum: 21.7.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
address letters to
Vikingpress, 18 East 48th Street
New York.
Ossining, July 21st, 41
Dear Manna,
Once in a while I must write a letter which
Stefan does not "censor" before I send it. I am a little
worried about him at present, he is depressed, not only
because it is really no pleasure to lead such an un-
settled life, always waiting {short-term} what will happen the next
day before making another decision, but also because
the facts of war which is now becoming a real mass
murder, and the seeming endlessness weigh upon his mind.
I hope this mood will pass soon and I wish I had some-
thing of those people who can talk others into cheer-
fulness and somehow inspire courage and hope. My qualities
are rather that I can stand any kind of life without
complaining and feeling sorry for myself, but I cannot
talk him out of his present mood and can only wait until
he gets over it himself - as he usually did in previous cases.
Fortunately this does not prevent him from working but in
the contrary induces him to more and more work. And I
hope that he will feel better when the decision which
has once again to be taken now between the States and
Brazil, has finally fallen. Both countries have their great
advantages - here are some really good friends of real
intellectual niveau, and the libraries, down in Brasil
life in itself is pleasant and interesting and the
country stimulating for Stefan. The people are extremely
nice and cultured, but cultured somehow in an old-
fashioned way, and intellectually there is a difference
of niveau so to say. - It is difficult to decide and
lots of things are to be considered - not the least the
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf weißem Papier. Tinte blau/violett. Gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
enormous distance and the fact that travelling with
all the necessary permits, visa and the journey itself
will probably become more and more difficult.
Sometimes we wish we were back in "Rosemount" in
spite of everything which made us leave it, and we
wonder sometimes whether this would not be the best
solution. Rationally it probably is not and probably Stefan
would again feel useless or be given an unimportant
job which others might do just as well, and besides
this it is nearly impossible to get home without special
official priorities. It is just a dream and only to be hoped
that one day circumstances will allow its realisation.
But it was not the reason of my writing to
inform you of our present mood - which will probably
have changed until you get this letter, so don't give
it much thought! - What I would like you to do
occasionally, is to get into touch with Cassell
(maybe you can get Newman Flower, the proprietor on the
phone) whether they are willing to send the manuscript
of Balzac to the Vikingpress (Mr. Huebsch). Stefan says
he does not want it, but I am convinced he will
be quite happy when he gets it or knows the Viking
Press has got it at his disposition whenever he will
have finished his present work. So please try to send
it - if possible through Cassell's because they have less
difficulties in sending a manuscript to another publisher.
Later on - better not at the same time as it is {as Balzac}
something quite different. I would like you to send me
a copy of the bibliography of Stefan's books. There are two
parts, one the printed book which is not quite so
important, and the typewritten additions which your

2
brother {typed out} for me in several copies. It would be
useful for me to have, and there is no special risk
of losing it as - just as in the case of the Balzac manuscripts
copies still remain with you. When you send this either
through Cassell or direct to me write clearly on it what
it is "bibliography of books published in translations etc.
by..." so that the censor sees at once what it is all about.
This is all what I have to tell you today.
And please don't worry because today I admit that
Stefan is passing through one of his black moods and
that we wish we were home and had never left. These moods
will happen once in a while and they will pass and when
you get this letter probably our plans for the next
months will be definite and we will feel better
accordingly.
We went to see Eva yesterday. She looks
and feels fine, loves Mrs Sch and Amity Hall and
Mrs Sch loves her. When you see her again you will
not find her changed at all, only grown and probably
a little more grown-up. I should hate to leave her
when we go really to Brazil, but only because I
shall miss her. She really is in excellent care for
soul, mind and body and is treated exactly as you
would treat her and has full confidence in Mrs Sch.
The new house they are taking is perfectly beautiful
and as Eva says "just made for them". -
One good thing is that we are not isolated
from friends here - Schaefers and Fuloep-Millers in
Croton, Stefan's first wife by pure chance also in Ossining
(as a matter of fact she was already here when we decided
to take this house) and the strange thing is that we are

almost on better and certainly more normal terms {with her}
with Stefan's brother who is absolutely egocentric. I
remember a conversation I had with you once with regard
to the relationship of first and second wives and husbands,
but it all seems perfectly natural and normal and
maybe the great difference in age makes it easier.
I like to think that you and Manfred
are now taking "holidays" in Bath and wish you an
uninterrupted pleasant time. Are there already
prospects for Manfred to get employment on account
of his new qualifications?
Love and kisses to both of you,
Lotte

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, die Handschrift von Lotte Zweig ist klar und deutlich. Nur wenige Stellen erforderten eine genauere Prüfung.
